findings.text: In thirty-five verses of narrative and saying (Gen 20:11, 1Sa 18:11, 2Ki 5:11, Psa 64:5, Jer 3:19, Luk 12:17 and the others) the thought is inner speech: the person says a sentence within, and the sentence is the thought, usually about what another will do or what will follow. The person does it, in the first person.

parts.grounds: Saul thought, Let me give her to him

findings.text: The thought held is shown wrong in the verse or the account: Abraham's no fear of God in Gen 20:11, Samuel before Eliab in 1Sa 16:6, Naaman's expectation in 2Ki 5:11, the father's in Judg 15:2, the Lord's hope of return in Jer 3:7, the ghost in Mar 6:49, the spirit in Luk 24:37, sleep for death in Joh 11:13, the errand in Joh 13:29, the vision in Act 12:9, more pay in Mat 20:10, the gift bought in Act 8:20.

parts.grounds: they thought it was a ghost

findings.text: Fear comes first and the thought gives its reason in Gen 31:31, Exo 2:14, 2Sa 14:15 and Job 32:6; in Neh 6:9 the enemies mean to frighten, expecting the work to stop, and in Luk 24:37 the startled disciples take what they see for a spirit.

parts.grounds: Because I was afraid, for I thought

findings.text: In Dan 4:19, Dan 5:6, Dan 5:10 and Dan 7:28 the thoughts themselves alarm the one who has them, and the color of the face changes: the thoughts work on the person and show in the body.

parts.grounds: his thoughts alarmed him

findings.text: The heart, or the mind, is named as where the thoughts are: in Gen 6:5, Deu 15:9, 1Ch 29:18, Isa 10:7, Jer 4:14, Mat 9:4, Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21, Luk 1:51, Luk 2:35, Luk 5:22 and Dan 7:28 they are of the heart, lodge within it, come out of it or are revealed from it; in Eze 11:5, Eze 20:32, Eze 38:10 and Dan 2:30 they come into the mind.

parts.grounds: out of the heart come evil thoughts

findings.text: Thoughts arise and lead out into acts: in Eze 38:10 thoughts come into the mind and a scheme is devised, in Dan 2:29 they come to the king in bed, and in Mat 15:19 and Mar 7:21 evil thoughts come out of the heart first, before murder, adultery and the rest.

parts.grounds: thoughts will come into your mind

findings.text: The thoughts of people are what the Lord knows, searches and discerns: in Psa 94:11, Psa 139:2, Psa 139:23, 1Ch 28:9, 1Cor 3:20, Eze 11:5 and Isa 66:18 he knows them, and in Heb 4:12 the word discerns them with the heart's intentions. The thoughts lie open to him.

parts.grounds: you discern my thoughts from afar

findings.text: In Mat 9:4, Mat 12:25, Luk 5:22, Luk 6:8 and Luk 11:17 Jesus knows or perceives the thoughts of those around him and answers them: their thoughts are what his knowing reaches.

parts.grounds: But he knew their thoughts

findings.text: In 1Cor 2:11 only the spirit of a person, within him, knows his thoughts, and in Ecc 10:20 even what is cursed in thought may be carried abroad: the thought is inward and yet not hidden.

parts.grounds: who knows a person

findings.text: The Lord himself thinks: his thoughts toward his people are many and deep in Psa 40:5 and Psa 92:5, precious to the psalmist in Psa 139:17, above man's in Isa 55:8 and Isa 55:9 and unknown to the nations in Mic 4:12; he thought to give Israel a land in Jer 3:19, he will do to Israel as he thought to do to the nations in Num 33:56, and he takes thought for the poor in Psa 40:17.

parts.grounds: my thoughts are not your thoughts

findings.text: What the thoughts are set on is evil in Gen 6:5, Job 21:27, Psa 56:5, Psa 64:5, Pro 15:26, Isa 59:7, Jer 4:14, Eze 38:10, Mat 9:4, Mat 15:19, Mar 7:21 and Jam 2:4: wrong against another, iniquity, an evil scheme, judging with evil.

parts.grounds: their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity

findings.text: In Isa 55:7 the unrighteous man is called to forsake his thoughts, and in Jer 4:14 Jerusalem is asked how long wicked thoughts will lodge within her: the thoughts are to be given up.

parts.grounds: the unrighteous man his thoughts

findings.text: In Isa 55:7 forsaking the thoughts leads on: the man returns to the Lord, who has compassion and pardons abundantly.

parts.grounds: let him return to the Lord

findings.text: Thinking is planning or intending in Isa 10:7, Jer 23:27, Dan 7:25, 1Sa 18:25, Job 6:26, 2Ch 13:8, 2Sa 21:16 and Phili 1:17: to destroy nations, to make the people forget the name, to change times and law, to make David fall, to withstand the Lord's kingdom, to kill David, to afflict Paul. The person intends an act.

parts.grounds: who think to make my people forget my name

findings.text: The thought is carried into the deed in the same verse: in Num 33:56 the Lord will do as he thought, in 1Sa 18:21 Saul gives his daughter as a snare, in Gen 32:20 Jacob sends the present to appease Esau, and in 1Sa 27:11 David leaves none alive.

parts.grounds: I will do to you as I thought to do to them

findings.text: Giving thought is attention of the mind turned to a matter: the psalmist thinks on his ways in Psa 119:59, recalls the Lord's rules in Psa 119:52, dwells on his steadfast love in Psa 48:9, and tries to understand in Psa 73:16; the prudent and the upright give thought to their steps in Pro 14:15 and Pro 21:29; the people of faith did not keep the land in mind in Heb 11:15.

parts.grounds: When I think on my ways

findings.text: Attention leads on: in Psa 119:59 thinking on his ways turns the psalmist's feet to the testimonies, in Psa 119:52 thinking of the rules brings comfort, in Psa 73:16 the thinking wearies until he goes into the sanctuary, and in Heb 11:15 keeping the land in mind would have given the chance to return.

parts.grounds: I turn my feet to your testimonies

findings.text: In Phili 4:8 the thinking is commanded and given its objects: whatever is true, honorable, just, pure, lovely and worthy of praise.

parts.grounds: think about these things

findings.text: In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem took no thought of her future, and her fall followed; in Ecc 9:10 there is no thought in Sheol. The want of thought is named as a lack.

parts.grounds: she took no thought of her future

findings.text: Thinking is a judgment of what is so or fitting: Judah takes the woman for a prostitute in Gen 38:15, a thing is unclean to the one who counts it so in Rom 14:14, the raising of the dead is judged incredible in Act 26:8, Paul judges what is needful in 2Cor 9:5 and Phili 2:25, and what seems best in someone's eyes decides in Num 36:6, 2Sa 3:19, Jer 40:4 and Jer 40:5.

parts.grounds: it is unclean for anyone who thinks it unclean

findings.text: The thought is turned on oneself: in 1Cor 3:18, 1Cor 10:12, 1Cor 14:37, Gal 6:3, Phili 3:4, Jam 1:26 and Luk 8:18 a person thinks he is wise, stands, is a prophet, is something, has grounds for confidence, is religious or has what he has; in Rom 12:3 one is not to think of oneself more highly than one ought.

parts.grounds: if anyone thinks he is something

findings.text: In Gal 6:3, Jam 1:26 and 1Cor 3:18 the self-view leads to self-deceit: the one who rates himself as something, being nothing, misleads himself, and the one who counts himself wise must first become a fool.

parts.grounds: he deceives himself

findings.text: The thought is asked of the hearer in Mat 17:25, Mat 18:12, Mat 21:28, Mat 22:17, Mat 22:42, Luk 10:36, Joh 11:56, Luk 13:2, Luk 13:4, Heb 10:29, 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5: what do you think, do you think. The question draws out a judgment the hearer forms.

parts.grounds: What do you think about the Christ

findings.text: The thought is forbidden or denied in Mat 5:17, Mat 10:34, Joh 5:45, Act 17:29, 2Cor 11:16, Est 4:13 and Isa 10:7: do not think, we ought not to think, let no one think, do not think to yourself, his heart does not so think. The verse corrects what would be thought.

parts.grounds: Do not think that I have come

findings.text: Where the thought is set against God it is a refusal: in Psa 10:4 the wicked man's thoughts say there is no God, in Rom 1:21 those who knew God did not honor or thank him and became futile in thinking, in Psa 50:21 they thought God like themselves, in Eze 20:32 the thought is to be like the nations, and in 2Cor 10:5 every lofty opinion against the knowledge of God is pulled down.

parts.grounds: they did not honor him as God or give thanks to him

findings.text: Where the thought is turned toward God it is a pursuit: in Psa 139:23 the psalmist asks God to search and know his thoughts, in Psa 139:17 God's thoughts are precious to him, in Psa 48:9 the people dwell on his steadfast love, in 1Ch 29:18 David asks that such purposes be kept in the hearts of the people, and in Psa 119:59 the thinking turns the feet to the testimonies.

parts.grounds: How precious to me are your thoughts, O God

findings.text: The thinking has a measure: mature or childish in 1Cor 14:20 and 1Cor 13:11, sober in Rom 12:3, the same mind or another in Phili 3:15, futile in Rom 1:21, and armed with Christ's mind in 1Pe 4:1. The words give the thinking its maturity or its emptiness.

parts.grounds: in your thinking be mature

findings.text: In 2Cor 10:5 the thoughts are taken captive to obey Christ, and in 2Cor 11:3 Paul fears they will be led astray from devotion to him by deceit: the thoughts are what is either brought under Christ or drawn away.

parts.grounds: take every thought captive to obey Christ

findings.text: In Job 32:6, Job 32:10 and Job 32:17 Elihu holds back his opinion out of fear and then declares it, and in Pro 18:2 the fool delights only in airing his: the view is held and spoken.

parts.grounds: let me also declare my opinion

findings.text: In Job 15:35, Isa 33:11 and Isa 59:4 what is conceived within is then born: trouble, chaff and mischief conceived, evil, stubble and iniquity brought forth. The figure joins what is formed within to what comes out.

parts.grounds: They conceive trouble and give birth to evil
